cards.title: Tumble Troll
cards.text: A troll that rides its boulder like the farmer on his hay bale, feet working the top.
cards.why: You said: "It would be fun if you made a troll variant that can walk on the boulders like the farmer on hay." Each part below is one piece of it with its film. Mark any part that is off.

parts.title: Its look
parts.text: Lean and gangly, arms out wide for balance, big hands and feet, long ears, a braid. Troll moss and nose.

parts.title: Riding
parts.text: It walks the ball along, feet stepping on top. Fast on a straight, wide arcs to turn.

parts.title: Rolling through you
parts.text: The ball throws whoever it hits out of its way; the troll stays up and rolls on, then comes round.

parts.title: Hitting a wall
parts.text: Into a wall: a crack, a chip off the ball, and it teeters, arms flailing. Your moment to hit it.

parts.title: Ball broken
parts.text: Break the ball and it falls off, dazed, then fights on foot for good.

parts.title: A whole fight
parts.text: Nothing staged: three heroes against it in the Warren.

cards.title: After it falls off
cards.text: Once its ball breaks it fights on foot for good. Or should it run, or find a new ball?
cards.why: Fighting on foot ends the fight cleanly and makes breaking the ball worth it. Running away drags fights out with nothing to do; a new ball would make it the rock troll's twin.

cards.title: Arrows hit the ball
cards.text: Shots at the troll hit its ball first. Fighters next to the ball can reach the troll.
cards.why: It stands on the ball, so the ball is in the way. Archers end up breaking the ball, fighters do both. The other way: shots fly over the ball and hit the troll.

cards.title: Where it lives
cards.text: The Pit, the Warren's third floor, with the troll and the rock troll. A bit rarer than them.
cards.why: It is a troll, so it lives where the trolls do. It is about as strong as a troll in tests.
cards.pick: The Pit, a bit rarer than the troll.
